clue.text: Strong words from dreadful-sounding people

indicators.note: the hyphenated 'dreadful-sounding' says only the spoken form of the word for dreadful is wanted

parts.note: dreadful means dire, which said aloud matches the opening of the answer
a people is a tribe

explanation.surface: Someone complains about harsh language coming from a frightful-seeming crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful-sounding' gives DIA, which said aloud is like DIRE (dreadful); then a people is a TRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a torrent of harsh, forceful language.

clue.text: Given bargain, books in for such surgery

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for books is placed inside the word for bargain

parts.note: a bargain is a deal
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A bargain is struck and medical texts are brought in for an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a standard crossword source for 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: Work on teeth is the kind of surgery described by this adjective, as in a dentist's practice.

clue.text: A short distance up

parts.note: in horse racing a head is a small winning margin

explanation.surface: A tiny gap is measured upward.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse that wins by a head wins by a small margin, the length of its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in a contest means leading, in front of the others.

clue.text: Aerosol explodes —— that's rash

indicators.note: explodes means the word aerosol is blown apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A spray can bursts, and someone remarks that was reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective meaning reckless, but it is a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseola is a rosy skin eruption, a type of rash often seen in young children.

clue.text: Helpful creature shows the way to get good marks

parts.note: a brownie is a household sprite in folklore that does chores at night
to point is to indicate direction, so points means shows the way

explanation.surface: A kindly sprite guides someone towards top grades.
explanation.walkthrough: In British folklore a brownie is a goblin who secretly helps with housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit earned for pleasing someone in authority is thought of as a tally of favour, good marks.

clue.text: Eventually, zip fastener is fitting

indicators.note: eventually points to what comes at the end, so only the closing letter of zip is used

parts.note: a roper is one who ties things up with rope, a fastener

explanation.surface: A zip fastener is, in the end, the appropriate choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eventually' takes the last letter of 'zip'. 'zip fastener' wants to be one item, but 'fastener' is a person who ties things with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and fitting are synonyms, both meaning suitable or appropriate.

clue.text: Soldier joins others to support corps in course of exercise

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting below, so the corps comes first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
GI is an American soldier
men are the other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A soldier teams up with comrades backing a military unit on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the soldier and others sit under RE, the Royal Engineers. 'Men' is the army term for other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed programme, such as a planned course of diet or physical training.

clue.text: Publicity on green conurbation showing early flowering …

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
eco means environmentally friendly, green
a city is a large urban area, a conurbation

explanation.surface: Publicity for an environmentally friendly city showing blossoms ahead of season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early flowering' looks horticultural but describes a child developing talents unusually young.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocity is development of abilities at an unusually young age, a figurative early blooming.

clue.text: … some radiation is not green, as it decays

indicators.note: decays means breaks down, as a radioactive substance does, so the letters of not green fall apart and re-form

explanation.surface: A radioactive material is no longer green once it breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decays' fits the radiation surface but is the anagram signal on NOT GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is a unit measuring exposure to X-rays or gamma rays, so it quantifies radiation.

clue.text: His Nobel amazing — gets to meet king

definitions.text: His Nobel amazing — gets to meet king

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishing or bewildered, so the words His Nobel are jumbled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A prize-winner's remarkable Nobel lets him meet royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the letters of HIS NOBEL ('amazing') gives NIELSBOH; then add R for king. The Danish physicist won the 1922 Nobel Prize and could well have met a king when receiving it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish physicist won the Nobel Prize for physics in 1922, which the whole clue alludes to.

clue.text: Huge antelope runs wild —— so does this

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of huge antelope and the runs abbreviation are scrambled

explanation.surface: A massive antelope charges about out of control, and so does another beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs wild too, so the clue's last words refer back to the wordplay's own phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue elephant is a lone, violent animal living apart from its herd that rampages uncontrolled.

clue.text: Turning say round notice, they'd want a gander

indicators.note: turning means the whole assembled string is flipped to read backwards
round tells us the abbreviation for say goes around the word for notice

parts.note: say, as in for example, is EG
to notice is to see

explanation.surface: Someone is turning round to spot a sign, curious to take a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gander' looks like 'a look' but is the male goose; 'Turning' reverses the whole container, not just 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is a male goose, so female birds of that species would want one as a mate.

clue.text: Decoration secured by prolific author: I say no more

indicators.note: secured by means the decoration is held inside the author's name

parts.note: Anon, the anonymous writer, is jokingly the most prolific author of all
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

explanation.surface: A medal pinned on a bestselling novelist, who then falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Anon is credited with countless poems and sayings, hence 'prolific author'. The DSO is a British award for military gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase trails off a list, meaning there is more of the same that need not be said.

clue.text: Spicy American dish's taken back to Wellington

parts.note: gumbo is a spicy stew from Louisiana

indicators.note: taken back means the short word to is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Cajun stew has been carried back to the New Zealand capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the city but is the wellington boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a rubber boot; in New Zealand and Australia it is often called a gumboot.

clue.text: Enjoy going to clean home ground that's strangely colourful

indicators.note: going to means the word for enjoy is attached after the rearranged letters
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of clean home are broken up and remade

parts.note: to enjoy something is to like it

explanation.surface: Someone likes heading off to tidy the family plot, which turns out oddly vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like land around a home, but it is the anagram signal: CLEAN HOME rearranged gives CHAMELEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes its skin colour, so something resembling one is oddly and changeably coloured.

clue.text: Felix's downfall, they say, an unusual event

definitions.meaning: Felix is a typical cat's name, and the proverb says nosiness killed the cat
an oddity or rare thing, a strange occurrence

explanation.surface: A cat's ruin is put down by gossips to a freak happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'curiosity killed the cat'; Felix is a famous cartoon cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiness proverbially killed the cat; separately, a rarity or oddity is also called by this word.

clue.text: Place for officers in fight, resistance overwhelmed by fate

parts.note: a war is a fight

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the resistance symbol is engulfed inside the word for fate

parts.note: doom is one's fate
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Officers' mess is described as a battle where opposition is crushed by destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: On a warship the wardroom is the mess and lounge used by commissioned officers.

clue.text: The first morning I may take you in

definitions.text: The first morning I may take you in

parts.words: The first morning I may take you in
parts.note: the first of a certain spring month, when pranks are allowed until midday, so the speaker may fool you

explanation.surface: An early riser offers you a bed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take you in' looks like giving shelter but means deceive; 'The first' is the first day of the fourth month, and the pranks traditionally stop at noon, hence 'morning'.
explanation.definitionFit: On the first of April people play hoaxes, taking each other in until midday.

clue.text: Italian sheets in sink in corridor

indicators.note: in means the word for sink is placed within the word for corridor

parts.note: a lane is a narrow passage or corridor
to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: Bedding from Italy is found in a basin in a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian sheets' looks like linen but is flat sheets of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is pasta in wide flat sheets, an Italian staple layered with sauce.

clue.text: Reduce pressure and scrub round

indicators.note: round means the word for scrub goes around the pressure symbol

parts.note: to scrub something is to cancel or delete it
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Lower the force and give everything a good scouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrub' looks like cleaning but means cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to diminish a stock or supply by using it up, lessening it.

clue.text: Creature from Iron Age reappears

explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Calls to repent

definitions.meaning: calls in the sense of pays a casual visit
to repent is to give up wrongdoing

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pays a casual visit pops round; split differently, the phrase means abandon wrongdoing.

clue.text: Music, sentimental stuff that may accompany film

parts.note: pop is popular music
corn is trite, sentimental material

explanation.surface: Chart songs and schmaltz, the sort of thing found in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Popped maize is the snack traditionally eaten while watching a movie at the cinema.

clue.text: Old slander crops up, covering one in blame

indicators.note: covering means the reversed slander goes around the figure for one
in a down entry crops up means the word for slander is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: mud is slander, as in mud-slinging
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ancient defamation resurfaces, one person getting the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crops up' reverses MUD in this down entry, and 'covering' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgrace attached to someone, the opprobrium of being blamed.

clue.text: Down from awful error on pitch, but securing three points

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the football error wraps around the result

parts.note: OG stands for own goal, a dreadful mistake on a football pitch
a win earns three points in league football

explanation.walkthrough: In football an own goal (OG) is scored into your own net, and a win is worth three points in the league table.
explanation.definitionFit: To be down is to be short of money that is due, in debt to someone.

clue.text: Desperately keen to keep jewellery, having invested pounds

indicators.note: having invested means the word for keep has had the pounds symbol put inside it

parts.note: to keep money is to save it
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (Latin libra)
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A greedy buyer, desperate to stash away precious items, has put money into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately keen' is the drooling sense: slavering literally means dribbling with eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavering means drooling with eager anticipation, hence wanting something very badly.

clue.text: Spring border in chaos

parts.note: May is a month in spring
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A flower border bursting with spring growth is in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem and chaos are synonyms for violent disorder and confusion.

clue.text: Flag in terrible cold?

definitions.meaning: a long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast
